newsitem.title: USA: U.S. withdraws some personnel at Freetown embassy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. withdraws some personnel at Freetown embassy.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it was cutting the number of American personnel at its embassy in Sierra Leone because of the unsettled situation following a weekend military coup there.
"The Department of State has ordered a drawdown of United States embassy non-essential personnel and dependents," department spokesman John Dinger told reporters.
"Contingency plans for an emergency evacuation, should that prove necessary, are also being developed," Dinger added.

He said the U.S. Navy helicopter ship Kearsarge, which has been ordered to head towards Sierra Leone, was expected to arrive there late Wednesday or early Thursday to stand by in case an evacuation was ordered.
Dinger said the embassy drawdown "seems to be a prudent measure to take given the unsettled situation" in Sierra Leone.
He said there were about 40 Americans attached to the embassy in Freetown. The department said Tuesday there were about 400 other Americans in the West African country.
